---
title: "Config"
---

The config file defines pipeline options that are not direct data inputs. Paths to raw data, project folders, or in-memory SpikeInterface recordings should be passed to the pipeline separately rather than encoded in the config.

## Scope

The config should describe processing choices, validation rules, and step-specific parameters. It should not define the location of the input data or replace explicit runtime arguments such as [`RAW_DATA_PATH`](outputs.qmd#raw-data-path), [`SPIKEINTERFACE_REC`](outputs.qmd#spikeinterface-rec), or [`PROJECT_PATH`](directory-definitions.qmd#project-path).

## Sections

Configuration sections to specify:

- Data loading options, including debug slicing and optional probe attachment.
- Raw data quality metric options.
- Artefact detection options.
- Preprocessing options.
- Spike sorting options.
- Postprocessing options.
- Curation options.
- Runtime and provenance options.

## Open Decisions

- Whether the config is stored as YAML, TOML, JSON, or a Python object.
- Whether every pipeline step receives the full config or only its own section.
- How config validation errors should be reported to users.
